title: Local bounded-above finite-free models of good lower truncations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,J,B,R,c$ and locally constant finite type have the meanings specified by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-site-locally-constant-finite-type]: $J$ is a precoverage containing isomorphisms and stable under composition and base change with the required pullbacks, $B$ is a commutative Noetherian ring, $R$ is its constant ring sheaf, and $c$ sheafifies the constant module presheaf along the ring unit. Let $P$ be a cochain complex of $R$-module sheaves with cohomology zero in sufficiently high degrees and locally constant of finite type in every degree [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For every integer $a$ and object $V$ there is a covering sieve $S$ on $V$ such that every arrow $U\to V$ in $S$ has a cochain complex $E$ of finite free $B$-modules, an integer $b$ with $E^j=0$ for $b<j$, and an isomorphism
$$(\tau_{\ge a}P)|_U\simeq c(E)|_U$$
in the standard derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of $R|_U$-modules. Truncation is good lower truncation [def-kun-truncations] and restriction is to the slice [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No lower term bound on $E$ or finite projective dimension is asserted.

proof.text: Apply the bounded truncation model theorem. On each arrow of its covering sieve obtain a bounded complex M of finite B-modules and its local derived isomorphism.

Every cycle of M is a submodule of the finite module M^j, hence finite by Noetherianity. Its quotient H^j(M) is finite by surjectivity of the homology projection. Above the upper term bound the middle term of the short complex is zero, hence its cohomology is zero. The homologyFunctorFactors isomorphism transports these statements to Q(M).
Apply the Noetherian pseudo-coherence criterion to Q(M). Unpack pseudo-coherence to obtain E, its upper term bound, finite free terms, and Q(E) isomorphic to Q(M).

Constant module presheaves preserve finite limits and finite colimits because evaluation at any site object sends their mapped cones to the original cone; module-presheaf evaluations jointly reflect limits and colimits. Compose with exact module sheafification and exact slice restriction. The resulting exact additive functor c followed by restriction induces a derived functor. Its representative factorization transports the derived isomorphism between E and M to an isomorphism between their realized restricted complexes.
Compose that isomorphism with the bounded model isomorphism on each arrow of the original covering sieve. The witnesses E and its upper bound prove the assertion.

theorem exists_site_finiteFree_truncation_models
    (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition]
    [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks]
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (𝓡(J.toGrothendieck, B))) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (P.homology j))
    (hlc : ∀ j : ℤ, IsLocallyConstantFiniteType J.toGrothendieck B (P.homology j))
    (a : ℤ) (V : C) :
    ∃ S : Sieve V, S ∈ J.toGrothendieck V ∧
      ∀ (U : C) (f : U ⟶ V), S f →
        let := HasDerivedCategory.standard (SheafOfModules.{u} ((𝓡(J.toGrothendieck, B)).over U))
        ∃ (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ) (b : ℤ),
          (∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (E.X j)) ∧
          (∀ j : ℤ, Module.Free B (E.X j) ∧ Module.Finite B (E.X j)) ∧
          Nonempty
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
                (((overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J.toGrothendieck, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex
                  (.up ℤ)).obj (P.truncGE a)) ≅
              DerivedCategory.Q.obj
                ((((cB(J.toGrothendieck, B)) ⋙
                  overFunctor.{u} (𝓡(J.toGrothendieck, B)) U).mapHomologicalComplex
                    (.up ℤ)).obj E))
